question_text:
(a) Calculate the fraction of atom sites that are vacant for copper $(\mathrm{Cu})$ at its melting temperature of $1084^{\circ} \mathrm{C}(1357 \mathrm{~K})$. Assume an energy for vacancy formation of $0.90 \mathrm{eV} /$ atom.
(b) Repeat this calculation at room temperature (298 K).
(c) What is ratio of $N{V} / N(1357 \mathrm{~K})$ and $N{V} / N(298 \mathrm{~K})$ ?

Give your answer as a tuple (the fraction of atom sites in (a), the fraction of atom sites in (b), ratio of $N{V} / N(1357 \mathrm{~K})$ and $N{V} / N(298 \mathrm{~K})$)
response:
## Solution

The equilibrium fraction of vacant lattice sites is given by the Arrhenius relation:

$$\frac{N_V}{N} = \exp\!\left(-\frac{Q_v}{kT}\right)$$

with $Q_v = 0.90\ \text{eV/atom}$ and $k = 8.617\times10^{-5}\ \text{eV/K}$.

**(a) At $T = 1357\ \text{K}$ (melting point):**

$$\frac{N_V}{N} = \exp\!\left(-\frac{0.90}{(8.617\times10^{-5})(1357)}\right) = \exp(-7.703) \approx 4.54\times10^{-4}$$

**(b) At $T = 298\ \text{K}$ (room temperature):**

$$\frac{N_V}{N} = \exp\!\left(-\frac{0.90}{(8.617\times10^{-5})(298)}\right) = \exp(-35.04) \approx 6.0\times10^{-16}$$

**(c) Ratio:**

$$\frac{(N_V/N)_{1357}}{(N_V/N)_{298}} = \frac{4.54\times10^{-4}}{6.0\times10^{-16}} \approx 7.56\times10^{11}$$

This enormous ratio (~756 billion) illustrates why solid-state diffusion is negligible at room temperature but becomes significant near the melting point.

$$\boxed{(4.54\times10^{-4},\ 6.0\times10^{-16},\ 7.56\times10^{11})}$$
